chapter_title: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive

questions.question_text: True or False: The Rajya Sabha has equal power with the Lok Sabha over Money Bills.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Think about the core principles discussed in Chapter 6.

solution_key.part_2_reasoning: False. Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
solution_key.part_3_conclusion: Conclusion confirms the validated NCERT answer.

questions.question_text: Trace the sequence of stages required for an ordinary bill to become an Act of Parliament.
questions.correct_answer: Introduction & 1st Reading → 2nd Reading (Clause Scrutiny/Committee) → 3rd Reading → Passage in House 1 → Transmission & Passage in House 2 → Presidential Assent → Gazette Notification as Act.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Think about the core principles discussed in Chapter 6.

solution_key.part_1_core_fact: Core Fact: Introduction & 1st Reading → 2nd Reading (Clause Scrutiny/Committee) → 3rd Reading → Passage in House 1 → Transmission & Passage in House 2 → Presidential Assent → Gazette Notification as Act.
solution_key.part_2_reasoning: Constitutional lawmaking requires thorough scrutiny in both houses of Parliament followed by executive assent by the President.
solution_key.part_3_conclusion: Conclusion confirms the validated NCERT answer.

questions.question_text: Explain how Question Hour, Parliamentary Standing Committees, and No-Confidence Motions enforce executive accountability.
questions.correct_answer: Question Hour forces ministers to publicly answer direct inquiries; Standing Committees conduct technical scrutiny of ministry spending; No-Confidence Motions allow the Lok Sabha to dismiss the government if it loses majority support.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Think about the core principles discussed in Chapter 6.

solution_key.part_1_core_fact: Core Fact: Question Hour forces ministers to publicly answer direct inquiries; Standing Committees conduct technical scrutiny of ministry spending; No-Confidence Motions allow the Lok Sabha to dismiss the government if it loses majority support.
solution_key.part_2_reasoning: In a parliamentary democracy, executive authority is continuously subordinate to legislative scrutiny and constitutional oversight.
solution_key.part_3_conclusion: Conclusion confirms the validated NCERT answer.

questions.question: Why is a Joint Sitting of Parliament permitted for deadlocks on Ordinary Bills but strictly prohibited for Money Bills?
questions.correct_answer: Because the Constitution grants supreme financial authority over taxation and expenditure directly to the directly elected Lok Sabha. Allowing a Joint Sitting on Money Bills would undermine the Lok Sabha's exclusive financial prerogative.
questions.explanation: Article 109 gives Lok Sabha final say on Money Bills; Rajya Sabha can only delay for 14 days.

hotspots.label: Bicameral Structure (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha)
hotspots.popover_description: Lok Sabha directly represents citizens (543 seats, 5-yr term); Rajya Sabha represents states indirectly (245 seats, permanent body).

hotspots.label: Lawmaking Process (Bill to Act)
hotspots.popover_description: Bill passes 3 readings in House 1, undergoes committee scrutiny, passes House 2, and receives Presidential Assent to become an Act.

hotspots.label: Executive Oversight (Question Hour & Committees)
hotspots.popover_description: MPs question ministers during Question Hour, review budgets in Standing Committees, and can move a No-Confidence Motion.
